sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the name Elokim is used in Yitzchak's blessing to Yaakov, and why the blessing includes Torah study which was already destined for Israel.

translations.translation: Now, it must be understood why it says "Elokim besides You,"
specifically the name Elokim.
And likewise, it must be understood in our portion,
the verse "And may Elokim give you of the dew of the heavens and of the fatness of the earth and abundance of grain and wine,"
and this is questioned in many places, and also in the continuation of the year 5666,
why it says Elokim,
for seemingly it should have said the name Havayah,
since the main aspect of blessings is specifically from the name Havayah,
and especially Yitzchak's blessings, which are most exalted blessings,
as explained in the Siddur at the end of Shaar HaTekios.
Also, it is not understood, as it is brought in Midrash Rabbah,
"dew of the heavens" refers to Scripture, "fatness of the earth" refers to Mishnah, "grain" refers to Talmud, etc.,
and it must be understood what is the concept of blessing him with Torah,
for seemingly a blessing for this is not applicable.
For the Torah was to be given to Israel anyway at the giving of the Torah,
since the primary intention in the creation of the worlds was for the sake of the Torah, as our sages said,
on the verse "In the beginning He created," etc.,
"for the sake of Israel who are called 'first,'" etc., "and for the sake of the Torah which is called 'first,'" etc.,
that the Torah was established in the nature of creation,
and in a manner of a condition, that when the condition is nullified, the thing is nullified,
and as it is brought in the Gemara,
on the verse,
"And there was evening... the sixth day,"
"The Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the works of creation: if Israel fulfills My Torah, etc.,"
and this is as it is written,
"From the heavens... the earth feared and was still," etc.,
"at first it feared, and at the end it was still,"
and if so, the giving of the Torah was a necessary thing, so how can a blessing apply to this?
Also, it must be said,
that whichever way you look at it,
if the intention of the blessing was for the study of Torah as it was before the giving of the Torah, surely no blessing was needed for this,
for there was already Torah study by the Patriarchs,
and as our sages said,
on the verse,
"And Avraham was old,"
"Avraham our Patriarch was old and sat in the study hall... Yaakov our Patriarch was old and sat in the study hall."
And also it cannot be said that the intention is for the Torah as it is after the giving of the Torah,
for the Torah of the Patriarchs
(which includes Yaakov as well)
was like a fragrance compared to the Torah after the giving of the Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section considers the possibility that Yitzchak's blessing of Torah was intended for Esav, but questions how it applies to Yaakov who actually received it.

translations.translation: And seemingly it could be explained,
that this was according to Yitzchak's initial thought,
when he sought to bless Esav,
and therefore he blessed him with Torah, thinking that through this he would be refined,
and for Esav a blessing for this is applicable,
because the Torah is only obligatory for Israel.
But nevertheless, it is not understood,
for in actuality the blessings were given to Yaakov,
and as it is written,
"Now he has taken my blessing,"
and they make of the blessings a great matter, etc.,
and according to this, it is not understood what is the concept of the blessing to Yaakov regarding Torah, etc.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Yitzchak's blessing was for toil in Torah, which draws from a level above the Torah itself, enabling the refinement of even the harshest impurities.

translations.translation: But the explanation is,
that the Torah as it was given at the giving of the Torah is the aspect of the Torah as it is in its own essence,
but Yitzchak's blessing was for the matter of toil in Torah,
about which it is said,
"He will do for those who wait for Him,"
and it is brought in the Zohar,
"those who press into the word of wisdom,"
that through this they reach a level above the aspect of the Torah as it is in its own essence,
for the Torah in its own essence is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and higher than that is the aspect of the Concealed Wisdom,
and through toil they reach the aspect of Eden, etc., about which it is said "No eye has seen," etc., as above,
which is entirely above the aspect of wisdom.
Based on this, Yitzchak's initial thought that he wanted to bless Esav so that he would be refined is also understood,
for seemingly how does this fit with the actual outcome
(and the Patriarchs are the Merkavah),
but rather, through the blessings that he blessed Yaakov regarding toil in Torah,
through this the power was given to refine Esav,
for since through toil they draw from the aspect of Eden,
therefore he can refine not only the kelipah of nogah but also the sparks within the three completely impure kelipot, etc.
And as explained elsewhere,
regarding "And Yaakov sent... 'I have sojourned with Lavan,'"
that then he completed the refinement with Lavan and went to refine Esav,
for Yaakov in his own essence was already prepared for this then,
and from Yaakov's side the refinement was then completed, etc.,
and this is through the blessings regarding toil in Torah.
